scenes.title: When recovery loses a customer
scenes.viewerPurpose: What happens when helping you get better means losing you as a customer?
scenes.composition: A person’s relief and a recurring bill occupy opposite sides of one uncluttered scene.
addOrChange: Add a simple seated person and a repeat-payment marker; remove the abstract question icon.

cues.visualAction: Let the need diminish while the recurring bill remains, leaving the tension visible.
Bring in the title with a small wry pause, without laughing at the person who needs care.

scenes.title: Three uncomfortable markets
scenes.viewerPurpose: Some needs are urgent, some feel too private to discuss, and others arrive at the end of life.
scenes.composition: Three modest objects stand for relief, privacy and unavoidable need.
addOrChange: Replace one/two/three labels with Relief, Privacy and Need; avoid medical claims or sexual imagery.

cues.visualAction: Reveal the three source metaphors in sequence, giving each space rather than a comic bounce.
Move attention from the objects to a person seeking help, keeping the objects subdued.

scenes.title: Relief that keeps you coming back
scenes.viewerPurpose: A useful service can bring relief while its business depends on the problem continuing.
scenes.composition: One person receives useful care while the service records another visit.
addOrChange: Replace the historical then/now comparison with a care visit and repeat contact; no invented clinical outcome.

cues.visualAction: Show relief as the person settles, then a discreet return-visit card.
Place an ordinary care contact and an AI companion conversation side by side with the same return-visit question.

scenes.title: The question behind the joke
scenes.viewerPurpose: Its jokes make room for questions that polished sales pitches tend to avoid.
scenes.composition: A phone pauses beside a person who has time to rest.
addOrChange: Remove the old clock loop and make the existing boundary represent a quiet break, not a diagnosis.

cues.visualAction: Let an insistent notification settle while the person looks away from the device.
Leave the person resting beside the open book; the product stays secondary.
